claims: Meet PRIMARY. Your business's brain.
A voice-operated AI command center that watches your pipeline, runs your follow-up, briefs you every morning at 7:05, and answers to its name.
Born inside a working Texas brokerage. Running live today.
Answers to 'Hey Primary' — or two claps — and talks back in a voice.
Morning briefing at 7:05 AM, pushed to your phone.
Automated nurture works your cold database daily, with instant human handoff the moment a lead replies.
New leads contacted in under five minutes, around the clock, weekends included.
Calendar invites by voice — sent only after you approve.
Email sent from your own address, signed in your name — and nothing goes out until you approve it.
Call notes drafted from speaker calls, posted only when you say yes.
Cold-calling games — Call Roulette, Hot Seat, Script Battle — feeding one persistent office scoreboard.
If PRIMARY can't verify a number, it says so. Every claim carries its evidence.
0 numbers invented. Ever.
4,400+ contacts live on THE FLOOR today.
150 nurture emails sent in one day — every one logged.
Runs a working San Antonio brokerage every day — and a cleaning company too.
Works for any business that books customers.
Follow Up Boss connects instantly; other CRMs by custom build. Every business can start day one with a simple import.
Your accounts remain yours. LDT operates with your permission, never owns your keys.
Campaigns are approval-gated and compliance-first. You own your list and your consent records.
A 20-person office pays under $90 per person.
Yes, it can talk. British accent included.
pricing: Team: $449/mo, $0 setup — 3 seats included, extra seats $79/mo each, up to 10 seats; 5,000 contacts included, +$50 per extra 5,000.
Command: $1,449/mo, $1,500 setup — 15 seats included, seats 16-30 at $69/mo, seats 31-50 at $49/mo.
Brokerage License: $2,450/mo floor, $2,500 setup, +$39 per agent, unlimited agents.
Add-ons: Social Media Management +$100/mo; IDX home search +$150/mo on the Website tier; custom CRM integration $500 one-time.

metaCloser.scope: generates the creative, writes the caption, schedules, posts, and scores performance
metaCloser.note: The closer rides SELF-MADE posts only (carousel/card/text_reel) and is the last line before the hashtags, after the primary CTA. It must never appear on an operator clip: a screen recording a human filmed was not made by PRIMARY, and the line would be false. Scope is exactly the `scope` string above — the bannedPatterns list mechanically refuses brand strategy, account management, and 'runs your brand', so a drifted line fails the gate rather than shipping. Wording rotates so consecutive posts do not close identically.

metaAngle.line: This post was scheduled and captioned by our own automation.
metaAngle.note: Deliberately worded 'our own automation', NOT 'the product it's about': the poster is LDT's internal pipeline, and PRIMARY the software does not run it — attributing one system's work to another is exactly the overclaim class this file bans. If Peter decides the auto-poster officially ships under the Social Media Management add-on, the stronger product-actor line can return; until then this is the version that is literally true. If a human ever writes or posts one by hand, the line must not appear on it.
